title: NASA Wants to Build a Base on the Moon
summary:
On March 24, 2026, NASA announced a $20 billion plan called "Ignition." The goal is to build a permanent base on the Moon and test whether humans can live beyond Earth for a long time.

NASA picked a spot near the Moon's south pole. Scientists believe water ice is trapped inside some craters that are always in shadow. The area also has places that get sunlight for long periods, which could help power a future base.

The plan has three phases. From 2026 to 2029, uncrewed robot missions will deliver rovers and science tools to explore the area and help find good spots for the base. From 2029 to 2032, NASA will begin building power, cargo and communications systems and early living spaces. Japan's space agency, JAXA, is developing a pressurized rover where astronauts could live and work while traveling far.

The third phase begins in 2032. It aims to create a permanent outpost where astronauts can live and work for long periods. NASA will add larger habitats, communications equipment and transportation systems. A nuclear power plant will also be built for steady energy during the long lunar nights.

"The moon base will help NASA learn how to live away from Earth, and possibly later to Mars and other planets," said NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman.
why_it_matters: It shows how space agencies plan big steps in stages, and how learning to live on the Moon could help people explore farther away.
